title: Hybrid warmup slice orchestrator and decode slip mitigator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: tail latency for interactive requests can spike when prefill and decode stages contend on kernel/kv bandwidth and when large prefills cause decode starvation. This PR introduces a hybrid warmup slice orchestrator that staggers small "warmup" slices to softly prime the KV cache and a decode-slip mitigator that enforces a lightweight pacing budget for decode-stage kernels. The two components are designed to operate together to preserve continuous-batching efficiency while reducing tail spikes and offering operators actionable knobs (warmup budget, slice width, kernel pacing target).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a WarmupSliceOrchestrator that creates short, high-priority prefetch slices for long prefill requests; these slices prime the KV cache for frequently hit keys without performing full decode work. Warmup slices are cancellable and have configurable budget per-request.
- Introduces a DecodeSlipMitigator that monitors per-GPU decode token throughput and inserts micro-yields (kernel pacing) when decode latency growth exceeds a windowed threshold. This prevents runaway decode kernels from starving pending prefill kernels.
- Exposes two runtime-config flags and one tenant-level tuning param: warmup_budget_tokens, warmup_slice_max_len, decode_pacing_target_ms. Values are surfaced in the runtime config and Redwood Console tuning UI (follow-up UI PR planned).
- Adds continuous-batching hooks so warmup slices are batched with prefill kernels when compatible; when not compatible the orchestrator uses a fast-path small-batch dispatch.
- Conservative defaults: warmup_budget_tokens=64, warmup_slice_max_len=16, decode_pacing_target_ms=4. These provided significant improvement in the internal perf benchmarks for mixed interactive workloads.

Benchmarks & results (internal perf harness, steady-state 24h runs):
- 95th percentile tail latency for interactive mix (median sequence length 64, 20% long prefill requests) reduced by ~32%.
- Median per-token CPU/GPU scheduling jitter reduced ~18% across the candidate cluster.
- End-to-end throughput maintained within 3% of baseline for 95th-percentile throughput configs (small loss due to micro-pacing but improved SLA stability).

Testing & incremental rollout plan:
- Unit tests for orchestrator scheduling logic and DecodeSlipMitigator heuristics.
- Integration perf test with the benchmark-lab harness (added bench script).
- Stage rollout: canary -> regional staging -> full main rollout. Operator flag gates included to disable warmup slices or disable pacing independently.

Related: ENG-3627 (smoother prefill-decode handoff), ENG-3690 (kv warmup strategy). This PR intentionally keeps the policy surface small; later PRs will add console defaults and more adaptive heuristics (entropy-aware warmup).

review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can you clarify how warmup slices are batched with prefill kernels? It looks like we might double-dispatch for small prefill+warmup cases.

Maya Chen: Warmup slices use a batching affinity token; when prefill kernels have matching affinity they get coalesced. If affinity mismatches, we use a fast-path micro-batch dispatch to avoid double-dispatch overhead.
Liam O'Connor: Mitigator heuristics look reasonable but we should avoid global timers per-GPU for scale. Suggest using the existing sched window sampler—see inline comment.
Maya Chen: Switched to scheduler window sampler for GPU-level throughput stats (addressed in commit 4). Removed per-GPU timer, replaced with sampler callback.
Sofia Alvarez: CI flaky with perf benchmark on first run, re-ran tests and verified stable results. Approving pending small doc tweak.
Maya Chen: Fixed doc wording and added console example. Thanks!
release_notes: Introduce WarmupSliceOrchestrator and DecodeSlipMitigator to reduce prefill-decode contention and tail latency. New runtime flags: warmup_budget_tokens, warmup_slice_max_len, decode_pacing_target_ms. No breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Operators can tune warmup_budget_tokens and decode_pacing_target_ms in runtime_flags; disable warmup via runtime_flags.warmup.enabled=false for safe rollback. Observe metrics kv.warmup_hits and kernel.decode_pacing_events to validate behavior.
